variants.headline: Business plan abandoned before opening
variants.sub: The planned {business} will not open: {founder} has given up the plan.
variants.body:
The founder {founder} has abandoned the plan for {business} before opening. The reason given is that {why}. The builder keeps what it was paid, and any grant is owed back. For {target}, the result raises a direct question about responsibility before an enterprise can begin operating.

The company never opened. The plan has ended, but that is not the same as turning the clock back. Keep the people behind the story in view, and ask the hard questions without inventing answers.

variants.headline: An intended company will not open
variants.sub: The business plan made by {founder} has been abandoned before the company opened.
variants.body:
The proposed {business} will not open: {founder} has given up the plan because {why}. Payments already made to the builder remain with the builder, while any grant must be repaid. Readers considering {target} should distinguish the end of the proposal from an ending without obligations.

The company never opened. The plan has ended, but that is not the same as turning the clock back. Keep the people behind the story in view, and ask the hard questions without inventing answers.

variants.headline: A household's business plan ends
variants.sub: The founder {founder} has abandoned the plan for {business} before opening.
variants.body:
The founder {founder} has abandoned the plan for {business}, with {why} given as the reason. It has ended before opening, but the financial consequences do not vanish: the builder keeps its payment and any grant is owed back. The stewardship of {target} deserves attention on that basis.

The company never opened. The plan has ended, but that is not the same as turning the clock back. Keep the people behind the story in view, and ask the hard questions without inventing answers.
